stem.en: Why do fishing communities often get a better catch at high tide?

text.en: Many fish move closer to shore for food and shelter

feedback.en: Yes. The fish come closer, so they are easier to reach.

text.en: The water is warmer, and fish swim up to the warmth

feedback.en: No. Warmth is not the reason. They come in for food and shelter.

text.en: The sea is calmer then, so nets are pulled more easily

feedback.en: No. A high tide is not always a calm sea.

text.en: Fish cannot swim as fast when the water is deep

feedback.en: No. Depth does not slow a fish.

explanation.en: During high tide many fish move closer to the shore in search of food and shelter, and this gives fishing communities a better catch.
